implementationPlan.description:
Lexer bookkeeping in packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts. The Lexer must emit exactly the tokens it emits today. Leave slash()'s regex/division choice, REGEX_KEYWORDS, CONTROL_KEYWORDS, the parens/braces stacks and the regexOffUntil guard untouched.

(a) Factor slash()'s prev test into a module-level operandMayFollow(p: Token | null). slash() calls it as `this.i >= this.regexOffUntil && operandMayFollow(p)`, a pure refactor.

(b) Add `readonly regions: { start: number; end: number; line: number }[]` to the Lexer. Record a region only when it crossed a line break (this.line > its entry line). Never record single-line chunks.
- templateText records { start: this.i at entry, end: j (the index of the closing backtick, of the `${`, or text.length), line: its entry line }.
- skipBlock records { start: this.i + 2, end: j (the index of `*/`, or text.length), line }.

(c) Add `firstRisk = -1`: the start index of the first token after which the lexer's view may disagree with a real parse. Set it once and never overwrite it. Candidates:
- (R1) Every slash() call, whatever the regex/division choice. That is every `/` in code that does not start `//` or `/*`.
- (R2) A `<!--` or a `-->` at a code position. Detect it in punct() before this.i advances.
- R1 and R2 count only when the rest of their line, from the token to the next breakLen terminator or EOF, contains a backtick, the two characters `/*`, or, while lexing inside a template substitution (braces.length > 0), a `}`. Reason: a regex or Annex-B misread never reaches past its own line, so without one of these it cannot flip template or comment state.
- (R3) A JSX-like `<` at a code position: operandMayFollow(prev) holds, or prev is the non-member id `default`, and the next character after optional spaces or tabs is an identifier start (isIdStart) or `>`. R3 is ungated, because JSX text spans lines.

(d) Linearity: answer the line-remainder question lazily, scanning each line at most once.
- Cache the end of the span you scanned, plus the last backtick-or-`/*` index and the last `}` index in it.
- A later candidate on the same line answers from the cache: lastHazard > i, or braces are open and lastBrace > i.
- Stop checking once firstRisk is set.
- Never ship a per-candidate rescan of the line: it is quadratic, and D6a times out on it.

Error handling: none of this can throw, and indices stay within [0, text.length].
implementationPlan.note:
Lexer bookkeeping in architectureRules.ts:
- (a) a module-level operandMayFollow(p). slash() is now `this.i >= this.regexOffUntil && operandMayFollow(this.prev)`.
- (b) readonly regions: Region[], pushed by templateText and skipBlock only when this.line > their entry line.
- (c) firstRisk = -1, set once through risk(gated). R1 is every slash() call. R2 is `<!--` or `-->` in punct(), checked before the index advances. R1 and R2 are gated by lineHazard. R3 is a JSX-like `<` after operandMayFollow(prev) or a non-member `default`, when optional spaces or tabs are followed by idStart or `>`; it is ungated.
- (d) lineHazard caches hazardEnd, lastHazard and lastBrace, so each line is scanned at most once. Checking stops once firstRisk >= 0.

implementationPlan.description:
Re-scan in extractImports (packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/architectureRules.ts).

(a) Widen ImportUncertainty.reason with 'ambiguous-syntax'. Document it on the interface: a line inside a multi-line template-text or block-comment region that would import if it were code. It is reported because an earlier lexing ambiguity means the lexer may have misread that region.

(b) Move the per-token recognizer loop out of extractImports into a private recognize(tokens) that returns { imports, uncertain }. Keep the logic identical.

(c) extractImports lexes once and recognizes. If lexer.firstRisk >= 0, take each recorded region whose start > firstRisk and walk its line segments: the opener-line remainder, each interior line, and the closer-line prefix.
- Split only at breakLen terminators: CRLF as one, CR, LF, U+2028, U+2029. Number lines from region.line.
- Re-lex each segment on its own with a fresh Lexer, then recognize.
- Flag the segment's line with { line, reason: 'ambiguous-syntax' } when it yields any uncertain entry, or any import whose specifier isRelative. An external specifier can never resolve into the tree, so it cannot change the outcome.
- At most one flag per line, including when two regions share a line. Track the last flagged line: regions and segments arrive in ascending order.
- Append the flags after the main-pass entries.
- Do not skip star-led lines (D1(10)).

(d) Update the Lexer banner comment. Strings and regexes recover at a line break; template and block-comment state do not. The re-scan reports such lines as uncertainty instead of passing silently. Name the residual the module still accepts: a misread can still hide an import on its OWN line.

(e) Error handling and purity:
- extractImports still never throws on any input.
- Exports are unchanged apart from the widened union.
- No IO, no Git, no module-level mutable state.
- evaluateArchitecture is unchanged: it already passes uncertainty through, sorts it, and ranks failed > inconclusive > passed.
- Stay linear: segments partition their region, and regions never overlap.

Run both architectureRules test files until green.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
extractImports never silently drops an import that its own lexing ambiguity hides on a LATER line.

After the first point where the lexer's view may diverge from a real parse, every multi-line template-text or block-comment region is re-lexed line by line. That point is either a JSX-like `<`, or a code-position `/`, `<!--` or `-->` whose line remainder holds a backtick, `/*`, or a `}` inside a substitution. Each re-lexed line that would import a relative path, or call import()/require() with a non-literal, is reported once as { line, reason: 'ambiguous-syntax' }.

So evaluateArchitecture gives 'inconclusive' instead of 'passed' for the six task repros, or 'failed' when a real violation is also present.
acceptanceCriteria: D1: all ten hidden-line texts give { imports: [], uncertain: [{ line: N, reason: 'ambiguous-syntax' }] } at the planned N.

D2: evaluateArchitecture gives 'inconclusive' with the file-tagged ambiguous entry for every D1 text, 'failed' for the bare require control, and 'failed' plus the ambiguous entry in the precedence case.

D3: there are no false flags without a risk point, before it, for single-line regions or for external-only lines. Dynamic or non-literal hidden calls are flagged. There is one flag per line, in ascending order.
D4/D5: line numbers are exact under CRLF, U+2028 and lone CR, and for regions left unterminated at EOF.
D6/D7: linear on the planned pathological inputs; never throws; every line is in range; the seeded corpus yields more than 0 flags.
The 133 landed tests in architectureRules.test.ts pass unchanged, and the file is byte-identical to HEAD.
invariants: The Lexer's token output is unchanged for every input.
extractImports never throws, and stays linear in the input length.
The module stays pure: no IO, Git or node: imports, no module-level mutable state, no new runtime dependency.
Existing uncertainty reasons and their lines are unchanged.
compatibility: The result shapes of extractImports and evaluateArchitecture are unchanged. Only the reason union widens.
V10 (task-db328cda, gated on this task) consumes the widened union as a named exit-2 reason.

A module-level operandMayFollow, factored out of slash() with identical behavior.
A private recognize(tokens), moved from extractImports with identical logic.
The extractImports re-scan of regions after firstRisk.
reuse: The existing Lexer and recognizer logic, run per segment.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Architect decision required by the task: add a new fail-safe uncertainty reason, 'ambiguous-syntax'. CQ-V10a's no-new-reason contract was scoped to V10a, and that task is DONE. Options rejected:
- Parser-backed extraction. typescript is only a devDependency; the daemon's runtime deps are chokidar, pino, pino-pretty and ws. A parser is a large new runtime dependency, and it still has to guess script vs module and JSX vs TS per file.
- Fixing the heuristics (default/extends regex keywords, Annex-B comments, JSX awareness). That changes V10a's frozen token output, and a lexer heuristic can never be complete. The re-scan does not depend on any heuristic being right.
- Always re-scanning every multi-line template or comment. It breaks the landed X4 case ('a multi-line block comment' expects uncertain []) and flags every code-gen template and commented-out import.
- Reporting re-scanned lines as real imports. An ambiguity must map to 'inconclusive', never to a false 'failed'.
- Tighter hazards: only up to the line's last `/`, or only after 'heuristic' prev tokens. Fewer risk points, but more logic and an enumeration QA can poke holes in. The rest-of-line hazard on every slash is sound for single-line misreads and simpler.
- Skipping star-led lines as JSDoc. That opens a bypass (D1(10)). Noise is limited by the relative-or-dynamic filter instead.

completionSummary:
Fix for the architectureRules lexer desync. A line hidden by a lexing ambiguity now surfaces as 'ambiguous-syntax' uncertainty, so the result is 'inconclusive' (or 'failed' alongside a real violation), never a silent 'passed'.

Runtime: architectureRules.ts, +121/-9.
- ImportUncertainty.reason gains 'ambiguous-syntax'.
- The Lexer records the multi-line template and comment regions and the first risk point:
  - every `/`, or an Annex-B `<!--`/`-->`, when the rest of its line holds a backtick, a `/*`, or (inside a substitution) a brace;
